question: at byte parity with GGUF Q6_K, does our recipe match or beat it -- i.e. is the 6-bit-class loss a byte gap rather than an engineering gap?

preregistration.why_this_matters: the prediction, the thresholds and the decision rule were committed and pushed before this conversion ran. This tool reads them back out of that file and asserts each threshold appears in its prose, so the verdict cannot have been chosen after the number was known.

registered_prediction.registered_headline_source: docs/29 L195, the figure already on the record

byte_law_at_q6k_surplus.derivation: hydrated 0.002700 / 3.73^0.397 = 0.001601. This is docs/29's ~0.0016: it charges the parity build Q6_K's byte surplus rather than its own.

byte_law_at_own_spend.derivation: the parity build spends 1448345600 bytes = 1.349 GiB over hydrated, which over ~25.6B quantized weights is +0.4526 bpw; 3.73^0.4526 = 1.815x, so 0.002700 / 1.815 = 0.001488
byte_law_at_own_spend.note: the parity build buys MORE bytes than Q6_K's surplus (1.349 GiB against 1.183), so its own-spend prediction sits below docs/29's headline.

role_share_bound.derivation: gate+up carry 77.1% of the sqrt-energy-weighted proxy error at hydrated widths; promoting them one bit divides that share by the measured MLP K5->K6 rung ratio 3.7390 (docs/37 §3.1), leaving a factor (1-0.7711)+0.7711/3.7390 = 0.4352, so 0.002700 x 0.4352 = 0.001175
role_share_bound.caveat: assumes the whole KLD scales with the weighted proxy error and that the un-promoted roles contribute no floor of their own. This is the most aggressive of the three and is registered as the lower end.

surrogate_scaled.derivation: sqrt_energy objective delta for gate/up K5->K6 is -2.7243; scaled by the two uniform role-group scales (0.000555, 0.000289) that is -0.001511 to -0.000788 on the hydrated mean.

registered_prediction.registered_consequence: every estimator predicts the parity build BEATS Q6_K's net-of-floor 0.001528 or matches it. The sharp pre-registered claim is therefore BEATS_Q6K or MATCHES_Q6K; MISSES falsifies the byte decomposition.

registered_decision_rule.BEATS_Q6K: measured mean < 0.001528 (Q6_K's net-of-floor estimate). Our recipe is better than GGUF Q6_K at equal bytes; the 6-bit-class loss in receipts/cross-engine-comparator.json was a byte gap and is now closed. Release candidate for a fifth repo.
registered_decision_rule.MATCHES_Q6K: measured mean in [0.001528, 0.002035], i.e. between Q6_K net and Q6_K measured. Indistinguishable from Q6_K at equal bytes once the cross-engine floor's own slack is admitted; still a release candidate.
registered_decision_rule.MISSES: measured mean > 0.002035 (Q6_K's measured upper bound). Q6_K is better than our recipe at equal bytes and the loss is NOT purely a byte gap; the byte-law prediction is falsified in magnitude and docs/29's decomposition must be rewritten.
registered_decision_rule.owner_override_on_preservation: the checkpoint is KEPT AND UPLOADED whatever the result -- owner priority, stated at scope-addition time.

headline: 0.001634 mean KLD [0.001541, 0.001742] on shard 0. At equal FILE bytes the K6-parity build lands BETWEEN GGUF Q6_K's net-of-floor 0.001528 and its measured 0.002035, i.e. MATCHES, and it does so while carrying 2.3062 GiB LESS transformer body than Q6_K.

the_prediction_and_its_miss.comment_on_the_headline: docs/29 L195's law-predicted 0.0016 is within 2.1 % of the measured value. That is the single most accurate quantitative prediction this project has made in advance.
the_prediction_and_its_miss.by_how_much_and_in_which_direction: the measurement is 0.0000328 ABOVE the top of the registered interval, i.e. the interval narrowly FAILED to contain it -- 2.0 % above its upper bound. Stated as a miss rather than reframed: the three estimators bracketed [0.001175, 0.001601] and the truth was just outside on the pessimistic side. The role-share bound (0.001175) was the least accurate of the three and the byte-law form at Q6_K's own surplus (0.001601) the most, which is the opposite of the ranking the surrogate calibration's scale spread would suggest.

what_this_settles.the_6_bit_class_loss_was_a_byte_gap: receipts/cross-engine-comparator.json recorded GGUF Q6_K as genuinely better than our best build at the 6-bit operating point. docs/29 L189-198 decomposed that as +0.397 bpw of byte surplus against a 3.73x-per-bit law and predicted the gap would close if we spent the same bytes. It closes: at equal file bytes the two are indistinguishable once the floor's slack is admitted.
what_this_settles.and_it_understates_our_side: receipts/cross-candidate-byte-accounting.json measures the body asymmetry. At this file size Q6_K carries 19.3599 GiB of transformer body against this build's, because our embedding is BF16 where theirs is Q6_K, our payload includes a BF16 vision tower their text file does not contain at all, and we ship an MTP draft they have no equivalent of. A match on this axis is a win on that one.
what_this_settles.what_it_does_not_settle: body parity is a separate and unrun experiment (attention K6->K7 on top of this recipe, about +1.4 GiB of body); the comparison is text-only teacher-forced fidelity on one shard; and the serving cost is real -- 21.45 GiB of payload is 1.35 GiB more than hydrated, which comes out of the KV budget on a 32 GB card.

paired_readings.versus_hydrated_same_engine_no_cross_eng: the parity build is better by 0.001066 [0.000974, 0.001173], winning 511 of 512 contexts. Promoting MLP gate and up from K5 to K6 cuts mean KLD by 39.5 % (0.002700 -> 0.001634) for +1.348 GiB of payload.
paired_readings.versus_gguf_q6_k_cross_engine: the parity build is better than Q6_K's MEASURED value by 0.000401 [0.000378, 0.000425], winning 493 of 512 contexts, with the interval excluding zero. Net of the measured cross-engine floor of 0.000507 the Q6_K estimate is 0.001528, which is 0.000106 BELOW our measurement -- so we beat the upper bound decisively and sit just above the naive lower estimate. KL is not additive, so the net figure is an estimate and not an identity, and no ordering that close should be pressed.

preservation_decision.decision: KEEP AND UPLOAD, unconditional and pre-registered as such before the conversion ran (owner priority). This is a release-candidate variant: it matches the best off-the-shelf 6-bit GGUF on our own suite at equal file bytes and beats its measured value outright.
